Historical May averages of 82–85 °F provide context, while ensemble spread allows for brief clearing that could push readings into the low 90s or keep them capped by rain-cooled air. Traders are therefore weighting the most probable model consensus while assigning smaller probabilities to drier, warmer outliers.

eventMetadata.context_description: Current forecasts from global and regional models, including runs from the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts, indicate mild Mediterranean spring conditions for Tel Aviv on May 20, with daytime highs most likely settling in the 24–27 °C range. Sea-breeze circulation off the Mediterranean is expected to moderate peak temperatures, while light westerly flow limits warm advection from inland areas. The tight clustering of market-implied odds across 23–27 °C reflects this narrow uncertainty band in the 24–48-hour guidance, with small differences in cloud cover or timing of the sea breeze able to shift the exact maximum by 1–2 °C. Historical May averages near 26 °C provide climatological context, but traders are watching the final Israel Meteorological Service update and any late model adjustments for resolution.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent model runs from Météo-France and the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts show a strengthening high-pressure system building over western Europe, driving gradual warming and reduced cloud cover for Paris on May 21.
